issue: Earlier artifacts promoted the January 2022 Kazakhstan targeted-filtering episode as confirmed foreign use of Russian-origin DPI. A later reverse-spiral pass recovered a materially conflicting public account about the equipment origin. The event remains relevant, but the Russian-origin attribution must be downgraded.

source_conflict.source: Freedom House, Freedom on the Net 2022/2023 Kazakhstan material
source_conflict.reported_claim: Later media reports indicated the government initially tried to use Russian deep packet inspection technology to impose more targeted filtering before escalating to broad shutdowns.
source_conflict.source_chain_note: Freedom House cites secondary media reporting, including Exclusive.kz/other local reporting.

source_conflict.source: Eurasianet, How did Kazakhstan shut down the internet?
source_conflict.reported_claim: Eurasianet, citing Forbes reporting and telecom sources, describes Israeli-made DPI equipment used for targeted blocking and attributes blocking commands/access to Kazakhstan authorities, including the National Security Committee/operator infrastructure.
source_conflict.source_chain_note: This materially conflicts with a simple Russian-origin device attribution while strengthening the local-control interpretation.

why_this_matters: The Kazakhstan episode remains evidence that a sovereign government can use centralized DPI for crisis-time targeted filtering, but it cannot currently serve as proof that exported Russian-origin DPI performed that filtering. This narrows rather than destroys the broader threat model.
interpretation_rule: All downstream summaries must cite this correction when discussing Kazakhstan 2022. Do not use the episode as evidence of Russian-origin foreign DPI censorship until the exact device/vendor lineage is independently resolved.

requirements: recover original Forbes/local reporting and any named vendor/model
search public procurement/operator disclosures for DPI equipment deployed at the relevant operators before January 2022
separate multiple DPI platforms that may have coexisted in Kazakhstan
identify which component actually executed targeted blocking
retain local-authority command evidence separately from equipment-origin evidence
